name: Peter Patel
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “My workshop changed when I learned to hold a chisel with my other hand.” On Wednesday, near the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio, Peter notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
voice: It fit my prosthetic thumb. For five minutes I remembered the weight of holding hands with a child.
appearance: Peter has a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow, a round face with a pronounced chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cream pullover. It usually goes with a little coil of soft measuring tape. When somebody else has the floor, Peter squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: Peter talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Peter's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To find a glove that feels as comfortable over the prosthetic thumb.
family: Bruno Gao is Peter’s cousin. Peter leaves the first voice message. Bruno calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The button card*, Bruno says, “I've been sewing pockets shut since my mother began losing coins.”
connections: George Crawford. The property photograph catches the patient discovering that the mitten will fit.

reactions.response: Peter saves the chair for a short agreed interval and checks who else needs it.
